messages:
anya: Heads-up: large enterprise customer asked for 1024-dim vectors (their search infra is fixed) and wants per-request batching up to 500 items with a 95th pct latency SLA of <250ms. They also asked about receiving raw float32 vs quantized. Can we support without breaking our current 1536-dim default?

kevin: @anya quick take: supporting 1024+1536 concurrently is doable but increases our model hosting variants. Memory/throughput tradeoffs on GPU mean we might need separate model artifacts (1024-quantized, 1536-full). 500-item batches at 1536 dims is heavy for a single GPU unless we batch across multiple slots.

maria: For prioritization: customer is strategic but not unicorn-level. Product ask is: define minimal compatibility (response shape + headers), latency SLOs for common batch sizes (1, 16, 64, 256, 500), and a migration story for clients pinned to 1024. Launch criteria should include backward-compatible response format.

sam: Ops/Platform constraints: we can't let a single tenant do unbounded large batches without quota. Suggest per-tenant max_batch=256 by default, with an opt-in increase to 500 for Dedicated/reserved customers. Also we should expose a rate-limit header and a per-request "effective_batch_size" metric.

kevin: Tech notes: two approaches for model selection: (A) single universal 1536 model and down-project to 1024 on CPU (fast but loses accuracy), (B) ship both 1536 and native 1024 models in the catalog and route by request param. Option B preserves quality but doubles artifact count.

anya: For API surface: proposal: keep embeddings endpoint (POST /v1/embeddings) with optional query param `?dim=1024|1536` and response field `vector_dim` to make clients explicit. If no `dim` provided, default=1536. Also add a header X-Embeddings-Model or return `model` in payload.

kevin: Sample response shapes we discussed:
```json
{
  "model": "text-embed-3-large",
  "vector_dim": 1536,
  "data": [
    {"id": "0", "embedding": [0.001, -0.12, ...]},
    {"id": "1", "embedding": [0.05, 0.3, ...]}
  ]
}
```
or compact form:
```json
{
  "model": "text-embed-3-large",
  "vector_dim": 1536,
  "embeddings": [[0.001, -0.12, ...], [0.05, 0.3, ...]]
}
```
Compact is cheaper to parse for many customers. We need to pick one for v1.

maria: Launch decision: prefer compact (`embeddings` array) to minimize payload overhead and match common client libs. But include `vector_dim` and `model` at the top level. Also expose `quantized: true|false` when we return int8/packed format. Those fields will be part of launch contract.

sam: Rollout plan: 1) implement param `dim` and response `vector_dim` + `quantized` flag. 2) soft quota default 256, opt-in increase to 500 via support. 3) canary 5% traffic, monitor metrics: p95 latency per dim, GPU mem pressure, E2E search recall (if customer test set available). 4) enable for Dedicated tenants after SLA verification.

kevin: Perf targets proposal: p95 <200ms for batch<=64 (1536), p95 <350ms for batch<=256 (1536) on hosted general tier. For 1024 dims expect ~10-15% faster. We'll publish perf-profile per model variant.

anya: Edge cases: what about customers sending mixed-dim requests? should reject with 400 if mixed dims in same batch. Also need clear error codes: 429 for batch too large, 422 for unsupported dim, 503 for temporary capacity fallback with `x-fallback-model` header.

embeddings-bot: NOTE: existing clients: 18% call embeddings with batch>64 today, 2% >256. Top customers using >256 are on Dedicated.

maria: Action items + owners:
- Finalize response shape (compact + vector_dim + model + quantized) — OWNER: anya — DUE: 2d
- Add `dim` param + server-side validation + 400/422 errors — OWNER: kevin — DUE: 5d
- Quota defaults & support workflows for opt-in 500 — OWNER: sam — DUE: 7d
- Perf profiles & docs page for model dims & perf numbers — OWNER: kevin + docs — DUE: 10d
- Canary plan + monitoring dashboards (p95 per-dim) — OWNER: sam — DUE: 12d

anya: Decision check: agree to compact format and `dim` param, default 1536, support 1024 at launch behind validation and quotas? :thumbsup:/:thumbsdown:

kevin: :thumbsup:
